name: Babol
classification_notes: Ultra-heavy display face built from soft, bulbous curves derived from 1960s hand lettering and psychedelic sleeve art; its rounded, swollen forms sit it in the bubble-letter display tradition rather than any text category.
summary: A four-weight bubble-letter display face with soft, swollen curves pulled from 1960s hand lettering and psychedelic sleeve art.
description: Babol swells every letter into a rounded, candy-bright shape somewhere between vintage psychedelic poster lettering and 90s pop graphics. Four weights run from an even-toned Regular to a loud Black, all sharing the same playful, bulbous character. A large glyph set with OpenType alternates and ligatures keeps repeat letters from looking identical across a layout.
foundry_blurb: Babol is a bold, ultra-heavy display typeface where every letter swells into a soft, bulbous curve, grown out of 1960s hand lettering and psychedelic album sleeves picking up 90s pop culture's candy-bright attitude.

name: Total 69
classification_notes: A themed five-family collection (Display, Stencil, layered Solid, Mono, and a 12-style humanist Sans) built around vintage football signage; grouped under display as the sans and mono components exist to serve the display concept rather than general text setting.
summary: A 21-style vintage football type system bundling display, stencil, layered solid, mono and humanist sans families under one release.
description: Total 69 packages five related families around the look of vintage matchday programmes and kit numbers: a sharp Stencil and commanding Display for headlines, a three-part layered Solid for crests and numerals, a four-weight Mono for stats, and a 12-style Sans with italics for running text. The range is built specifically for sports branding and retro editorial work rather than general use.
foundry_blurb: A full-stadium typographic menu serving up the golden era of football, a modern-retro spread of 21 fonts across five matching families crafted to feel nostalgic and bold in equal measure.

name: Stretch and Bleed
classification_notes: A squeezed, condensed grotesque sans paired with a textured ink-bleed companion; the condensed, high-contrast proportions place it in brutalist grotesque territory.
summary: A dual-family condensed grotesque pairing a sharp eight-weight Clean cut with a five-weight ink-bleed companion for textured retro-brutalist layouts.
description: Stretch and Bleed offers a squeezed, melodramatic sans-serif (Stretch Clean, 8 weights from Thin to Extra Bold) alongside a heavier ink-bled counterpart (Stretch Bleed, 5 weights) that mimics ink soaking into porous paper. Together the two families move between razor-sharp brutalist clarity and a rougher, textured retro finish.
foundry_blurb: A striking dual-family typeface balancing brutalist raw edges with the tactile warmth of vintage printing, offering both razor sharp clarity and ink-soaked nostalgia.

name: Basepath
classification_notes: A five-part themed set (Script, Slab, Condensed, two Tuscans) built around vintage American baseball signage; catalogued under display since the set exists as a decorative ensemble rather than a single text family.
summary: A five-font vintage baseball type system pairing a decorative script with a slab, a condensed sans and two ornamental Tuscan display faces.
description: Basepath draws on vintage American baseball tickets, posters and labels, splitting the concept across five companion fonts: a Script with alternates and decorative tails, a Slab, a lean Condensed, and two Tuscan display styles. It's built for branding and event work that wants a modern take on ballpark nostalgia rather than any single running-text use.
foundry_blurb: A modern retro spread of five delicious fonts serving up a nostalgic feast inspired by vintage American baseball tickets, posters and labels, crafted to feel timeless and bold.

name: Neutral
classification_notes: An 18-weight geometric Neo-Grotesque with close apertures and matching italics; a conventional text-and-display grotesque rather than a display novelty.
summary: An 18-weight geometric Neo-Grotesque with matching italics and close apertures, built as a dependable general-purpose workhorse rather than a display statement.
description: Neutral is Aiyari's plain, load-bearing sans: nine weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, giving 18 styles in total. Close apertures keep small sizes legible, while stylistic alternates offer some room for a designer's own voice without disturbing the family's essentially quiet character.
foundry_blurb: A geometric Neo-Grotesk that delivers clarity and purpose, with 18 weights and matching italics offering structure and flexibility, close apertures for legibility, and stylistic alternates for a touch of freedom.

name: Rooted
classification_notes: A single-weight angular display face styled after vintage horror and adventure comic covers; its hand-carved, deliberately imperfect forms place it firmly in display use.
summary: A single-weight angular display face channelling vintage horror and adventure comic-cover lettering.
description: Rooted takes its sharp, deliberately imperfect angles from classic horror and adventure comic covers, aiming for a hand-carved, retro-grit feel rather than clean modern construction. It suits flyers, movie titling and branding work that wants an unpolished, era-specific character.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by vintage comic covers, Rooted brings raw power and retro grit with sharp, angular forms that channel a hand-carved feel and deliberate imperfection.

name: Psych Fonts Collection
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Aprian Sembada, Cecep Nur Rohim
classification_notes: Four unrelated single-weight display faces (Liquid, Tangerines, Meicxel, Skarn) sold as one themed collection exploring psychedelic letterform treatments, from fluid and blobby to sharp and ornamental.
summary: A four-font collection of unrelated psychedelic display faces, ranging from fluid and blobby to sharp and ornamental.
description: The Psych collection bundles four distinct display typefaces exploring psychedelic design through contemporary letterforms, each treating the brief differently rather than sharing a common construction. It suits expressive branding, poster art and album cover work looking for a nostalgic-modern psychedelic register.
foundry_blurb: A curated set of four display typefaces exploring the expressive spirit of psychedelic design through contemporary forms, from fluid and blobby to sharp and ornamental.

name: Gipse
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Aprian Sembada, Cecep Nur Rohim
classification_notes: A bold, chunky display face with rounded counters and exaggerated proportions recalling 1930s vintage comics; the Oblique companion functions as its italic-style cut.
summary: A bold, chunky display face with rounded, geometric letterforms recalling 1930s vintage comics.
description: Gipse leans on thick strokes and irregular proportions to recreate a mid-century comic feel, mixing sharp and soft angles across a single heavy weight and its oblique companion. It's built for posters and logotypes rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: A bold, retro-inspired display typeface with chunky, geometric letterforms bringing the charm of 1930s vintage comics, reminiscent of mid-century modern typography with exaggerated proportions.

name: Gothedge
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Cecep Nur Rohim, Aprian Sembada
classification_notes: An ultra-condensed, tall display face with curving Art Nouveau details across seven weights and matching italics; built for headline impact rather than text setting.
summary: An ultra-condensed, tall display face across seven weights and italics, blending clean streamlined forms with Art Nouveau curves.
description: Gothedge stretches its letterforms tall and narrow, then works Art Nouveau curling details into an otherwise clean construction. Seven weights with matching italics give it more range than most display faces of this kind, though its condensed proportions keep it to headline and logotype use.
foundry_blurb: A striking typeface that seamlessly blends the elegance of clean, streamlined letterforms with the playful spirit of Art Nouveau, its ultra-condensed, tall letterforms ideal for refined elegance and avant-garde creativity.

name: Starlit Night
classification_notes: A two-style set pairing a flare-serif display face with a humanist sans companion, both drawing on 1960s-70s lettering; grouped as display given the pairing is headline-oriented.
summary: A two-style retro pairing of a flare-serif display face and a humanist sans companion, drawn from 1960s-70s lettering.
description: Starlit Night blends distinctive flare serifs with humanist letterforms for a warm, approachable retro feel, offered as a Display style for headlines alongside a plainer Sans companion for supporting text.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by 60s-70s lettering, Starlit Night seamlessly blends nostalgia with a modern aesthetic through distinctive flare serifs and humanist letterforms for a warm, approachable feel.

name: The Polish
classification_notes: A rounded old-style serif evolved from the foundry's earlier Beardy design, with 60s-70s pop flourishes; its serif construction and old-style proportions place it in the serif category despite display-oriented use.
summary: A retro-inspired, rounded old-style serif evolved from the foundry's earlier Beardy design, mixing 60s-70s pop flourishes with elegant detailing.
description: The Polish rounds off an old-style serif skeleton with playful 60s-70s pop culture flourishes, building on the foundry's earlier Beardy typeface. Fifteen stylistic-set variations (Ss01-Ss15) give it enough alternate flourishes for headline and logotype work.
foundry_blurb: A retro-inspired, rounded old-style serif typeface evolving from the beloved Beardy font, merging the playful spirit of 60s-70s pop culture with elegant flourishes.

name: Bytebit
classification_notes: A two-style pairing of a blocky pixel-edged sans and a matching script, styled after 90s computer interfaces; grouped as display given its novelty, headline-only character.
summary: A retro-futuristic pairing of a blocky, pixel-edged sans and companion script styled after 90s computer interfaces and arcade culture.
description: Bytebit takes its bold, blocky aesthetic from 90s computer interfaces, pairing a pixel-perfect Sans with a matching Script style for a nostalgic arcade-and-early-internet feel.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by 90s computer interfaces and pop culture, Bytebit combines retro-futuristic edges with pixel-perfect construction to evoke the nostalgia of arcade games, neon colours and early internet typography.

name: Sunkits
classification_notes: A single-weight bubble display face mixing hobo-style lettering with a psychedelic vintage sensibility; a headline-only novelty face.
summary: A single-weight bubble display face blending hobo-style lettering with a groovy, psychedelic vintage sensibility.
description: Sunkits leans heavily on the hobo lettering tradition, rounding it out with a bubble vintage letterform and a psychedelic design approach for headline and logo work with a groovy 70s tone.
foundry_blurb: Heavily influenced by hobo typeface infused with bubble vintage letterform with a psychedelic design approach, encompassing everything needed for a modern groovy creative project.

name: Globey
classification_notes: A single-weight bubble letterform display face with a large ligature set, aimed at eye-catching headline use rather than text.
summary: A playful vintage bubble-letter display face with an unusually large ligature set of 676 combinations.
description: Globey blends a vintage bubble letterform with a modern playful finish, backed by 676 ligatures to keep repeated letter pairs varied across headline and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Influenced by vintage bubble letterforms, Globey seamlessly blends a modern aesthetic with a playful approach, adding an eye-catching flair while keeping visuals fresh and lively.

name: Cringe
classification_notes: A five-weight calligraphic display face combining uncial letterforms with psychedelic pop styling; the rounded, brush-like uncial construction sits it closer to display than conventional script.
summary: A five-weight calligraphic display face pairing uncial letterforms with a psychedelic pop-culture finish.
description: Cringe combines an uncial letter structure with free-spirited calligraphic strokes, running from a plain Regular through Medium, DemiBold and Bold to a wider Expanded cut. Stylistic sets and ligatures back up its whimsical, psychedelic character.
foundry_blurb: A captivating typeface drawing inspiration from psychedelic pop culture combined with an uncial letterform and calligraphy approach, with each character exuding whimsy and free-spiritedness.

name: Thrope
classification_notes: A three-weight irregular display face directly influenced by Motter Ombra, with a basic geometric shape reworked for 60s-70s pop character; a headline face rather than a text sans.
summary: An irregular retro display face across three weights, heavily influenced by Motter Ombra and 60s-70s pop culture.
description: Thrope reworks a basic geometric letterform with irregular, hand-adjusted details, taking its cue directly from the Motter Ombra typeface. Three weights and four sets of stylistic alternates keep it flexible for logotype and headline work.
foundry_blurb: The Irregular Retro Display Font Family, heavily influenced by Motter Ombra typeface, geometric basic shape, and 60s to 70s pop culture.

name: Blufy
classification_notes: A two-style balloon-lettering display face drawing heavily on Cooper Black and 60s-70s hand lettering; its soft, swollen serif detailing puts it in display rather than text serif use.
summary: A soft, balloon-lettering display face drawing on Cooper Black and 60s-70s hand-lettered signage.
description: Blufy softens its serif construction into rounded, balloon-like forms borrowed from Cooper Black and mid-century hand lettering, offered in Regular and Oblique with ten stylistic sets and swash alternates.
foundry_blurb: A new softest retro font family, heavily influenced by Cooper Black typeface and balloon hand lettering from the 60s-70s era.

name: Tropika Island
classification_notes: A three-style set pairing an interlocking tiki-signage display face with an italic and a companion script; classed as display given its Mid-Century Tiki Art signage source.
summary: A tropical display type family built around an interlocking tiki-signage face, its italic, and a companion script.
description: Tropika Island continues the foundry's earlier Dreadful and Saturday Night designs, reworked around Mid-Century Tiki Art signage. The Interlock face carries over 3,200 ligature pairs for joined lettering, while Tropika Script provides a looser companion for secondary lines.
foundry_blurb: A new Tropical Display Font Family inspired by previous typefaces combined with Midcentury Tiki Art Signage, featuring Tropika Interlock with thousands of ligature pairs and a complementary Tropika Script.

name: Laguna Vintage
classification_notes: A 29-style variable display family modelled on American motor-inn and roadside restaurant signage from the 1950s-70s; a decorative signage face rather than a text design.
summary: A 29-style variable display face modelled on American motor-inn and roadside restaurant signage from the 1950s-70s.
description: Laguna Vintage takes its cue from mid-century American motor-inn signs, offered as a large weight range plus a variable font build and a set of matching graphic extras. Stylistic sets, contextual alternates and ligatures support headline and logotype work in that register.
foundry_blurb: Inspired from American motor inn signs and vintage restaurant signs in the 50s-70s, Laguna comes with stylistic alternates, stylistic sets, contextual alternates and ligatures, also available in variable font format with graphic extras.

name: Spooktacular
subcategory: beatnik horror serif and companion sans
classification_notes: A 15-style set built around a seven-weight serif inspired by the beatnik movement and vintage horror comics, paired with a companion Spooky Sans family; classed as display given its novelty, illustrative character.
summary: A 15-style horror-and-beatnik type family pairing a seven-weight serif with a companion Spooky Sans, finished with doodle dingbats.
description: Spooktacular fuses the 1950s beatnik movement with vintage horror-movie and comic references across seven serif weights, backed by a matching Spooky Sans family for supporting text and a set of doodle dingbats for extra decoration.
foundry_blurb: The fusion of the beatnik movement of the 1950s, vintage horror movies, and vintage comics, offering the magic of contextual and stylistic alternates plus extra doodle dingbats to perfect the design.

name: Lucidity
classification_notes: A six-style groovy psychedelic display set comprising three Psych treatments (Regular, Outline, Expand), a Condensed companion, and two extras faces; grouped under display for its novelty, era-specific character.
summary: A groovy psychedelia-era display trio with matching outline and expanded cuts, a condensed companion and two extras faces.
description: Lucidity embraces the psychedelia era with a modern touch, spreading across a core Psych face plus Outline and Expand treatments, a Condensed companion for tighter settings, and two supporting Extras faces of dingbats and ornaments.
foundry_blurb: A new groovy font trio embracing the psychedelia era combined with a modern touch, featuring stylistic alternates and ligatures.

name: Winter Is Coming
classification_notes: A five-style hand-lettered seasonal set spanning a Serif (with Expand and Shadow cuts) and a companion Script (with a Shadow cut), plus an Extra ornaments face; grouped as display given its decorative, seasonal brief.
summary: A playful hand-lettered winter type set spanning a serif family with shadow and expanded cuts, a companion script, and a bonus ornaments face.
description: Winter Is Coming reworks 1950s-60s winter hand lettering into five companion styles: a core Serif with Expand and Shadow variants, a matching Script with its own Shadow cut, and an Extra face of seasonal ornaments and graphics.
foundry_blurb: A new playful font family inspired by hand lettering at the winter season in 1950-1960, containing five collections of fonts with stylistic alternates, stylistic sets, ornaments and ligatures, plus a bonus graphic package.

name: Lovadelic
classification_notes: A five-style retro script built from 70s script lettering mixed with psychedelic balloon typography; its joined, hand-lettered forms place it in the script category despite display-scale use.
summary: A five-style retro script combining 70s script lettering with psychedelic balloon typography, including expanded and slanted cuts.
description: Lovadelic takes 70s script lettering and rounds it into psychedelic balloon-style forms, with Expand and Slant variants (plus a slanted Expand) offering more headline flexibility. An Extras face of matching graphics rounds out the set.
foundry_blurb: A new retro script inspired by 70s script lettering combined with psychedelic balloon typography, coming with stylistic alternates, stylistic sets, contextual alternates and ligatures plus extras graphics.

name: The Moonlight
classification_notes: A two-style handwritten script modelled on ball-pen lettering with an 80s-90s tone; a Swash companion supplies decorative connecting flourishes.
summary: A ball-pen handwritten script in Clean and Swash cuts, with an 80s-90s retro tone.
description: The Moonlight mimics loose ball-pen handwriting rather than a formal calligraphic script, offered in a plain Clean style and a Swash companion with extra connecting flourishes. PUA-encoded alternates support more elaborate layouts.
foundry_blurb: A new handwritten font inspired by ball pen handwriting combined with an 80s-90s nuance, supporting stylistic alternates, stylistic sets, ligatures and PUA-encoded glyphs.

name: Dreadful
classification_notes: A four-to-five-style layered horror display face meant to be stacked (Regular, Rot, Rust, Shadow) with a matching Extras face; a stacking display system rather than a weight progression.
summary: A layered horror-comic display face with Rot, Rust and Shadow variants designed to be stacked for a decayed, decrepit finish.
description: Dreadful is built from classic horror movie and vintage comic references, with Rot, Rust and Shadow layers meant to be combined over the base Regular for a distressed, decaying effect, plus an Extras face of matching graphics.
foundry_blurb: A new layered typeface inspired by classic horror movies and vintage comics, suited to film titles, album covers, logos and other applications wanting a haunted, decayed character.

name: The Painter
classification_notes: A two-style hand-lettered brush script drawn from traditional sign painting; its brushed, joined strokes place it in the script category.
summary: A hand-lettered brush script drawn from traditional sign painting, in a Clean cut and a distressed Rust companion.
description: The Painter recreates traditional sign-painter brush lettering, offered as a plain Clean style and a rougher Rust cut, both carrying contextual and stylistic alternates plus swash finals for more expressive sign-offs.
foundry_blurb: A hand lettering typeface inspired by traditional sign painting and brush lettering, coming in Regular and Rusty styles with contextual alternates, stylistic sets, ligatures, finals and swash.

name: Minority
classification_notes: A single-style hand-painted script drawing on street art and graffiti lettering rather than a formal calligraphic model.
summary: A hand-painted script drawing on street art, graffiti and 90s grunge lettering.
description: Minority combines a condensed hand-lettering skeleton with a graffiti and street-art sensibility, aimed at branding and apparel work that wants a raw, sprayed-on character rather than a polished script.
foundry_blurb: A hand painted script inspired by condensed typeface and hand lettering typography, combined with street art, graffiti, grunge, pop culture and 90s nuance.

name: Fabulous
classification_notes: A single-style monoline script with an even stroke weight, drawing on vintage and retro lettering conventions.
summary: A hand-made monoline script with a vintage, retro-leaning character.
description: Fabulous keeps a single even stroke weight throughout, giving it a cleaner, more restrained retro feel than the foundry's bolder scripts. It suits logo and packaging work looking for a light hand-lettered touch.
foundry_blurb: A hand-made monoline script inspired by vintage and retro culture with a modern touch.

name: Embers
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Cecep Nur Rohim, Aprian Sembada
classification_notes: A single-weight display face with pronounced inktraps on horizontal and vertical strokes, built for large-size headline use; the exaggerated ink-trap detailing marks it as a display rather than text design.
summary: A single-weight display face with extra-large inktraps, mixing Art Nouveau influence with a modern, experimental edge.
description: Embers is built for headlines in large sizes, using an exaggerated inktrap on both horizontal and vertical strokes to capture a vintage Art Nouveau nuance with a modern twist. Ten stylistic sets and ligatures extend its decorative range.
foundry_blurb: Heavily influenced by art nouveau design and combined with a modern, experimental approach, Embers uses an extra big inktrap on horizontal and vertical forms to capture vintage nuance with a modern twist.

name: Thunderstorm
classification_notes: A two-style hand-made brush script drawing on 80s-90s music and grunge culture; Brush and Monoline cuts both retain a hand-lettered, joined character.
summary: A hand-made brush script in Brush and Monoline cuts, drawing on 80s-90s music, disco and grunge culture.
description: Thunderstorm is built as a loose, energetic brush script referencing 80s-90s music and pop culture, with a textured Brush cut and a cleaner Monoline companion for calmer settings.
foundry_blurb: A hand-made brush typeface inspired by 80s-90s music, retro, disco and grunge, and pop culture.

name: Violence
classification_notes: A single-style hand-drawn brush script with a deliberately messy, urgent character drawn from riot and protest imagery.
summary: A hand-drawn brush script with a deliberately messy, urgent character taken from riot and protest imagery.
description: Violence pairs a chaotic, hand-drawn brush stroke with a raw, unfinished finish to read as instant and messy rather than composed, suited to posters and branding wanting a confrontational tone.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by chaotic, riot, protest and amok nuance, combined with hand-drawn brush strokes that make the typeface look instant and messy.

name: Romns
classification_notes: A three-weight display-leaning sans drawing on Roman letterforms with Art Deco and Art Nouveau influence; its humanist sans-serif construction places it in the sans category.
summary: A three-weight sans-serif inspired by Roman letterforms, blending Art Deco and Art Nouveau influence with a humanist sans structure.
description: Romns takes the elegance of Roman letterforms and reworks it through Art Deco and Art Nouveau detailing over a humanist sans-serif base, running Light, Regular and Bold. Its refined, slightly nostalgic character suits logotypes and packaging over long-form text.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface inspired by the elegance of Roman letterforms, seamlessly blending Art Deco and Art Nouveau movements with a touch of modernism and humanist sans-serif aesthetics.

name: The Beardy
classification_notes: A single-style rounded old-style serif, later developed into the foundry's The Polish; its serif proportions and old-style skeleton place it in the serif category.
summary: A rounded old-style serif that later formed the basis for the foundry's The Polish typeface.
description: The Beardy is a single-weight rounded serif with a retro character, later reworked and extended into The Polish. It suits headline and logotype use where a softened old-style serif reads warmer than a formal text face.
foundry_blurb: A rounded old-style serif typeface with a retro character, the starting point for the foundry's later Polish design.

name: Saturday Night
classification_notes: A seven-style disco-era set built around an interlocking display face (Regular, Hollow, Expand, Shadow) paired with a companion Script (Regular, Shadow); grouped as display given its headline, signage-style brief.
summary: A seven-style disco-era type family pairing an interlocking display face with a companion script, each in multiple decorative cuts.
description: Saturday Night channels 70s-80s disco lettering through an Interlock display face (with Hollow, Expand and Shadow variants) and a matching Script (plain and Shadow), backed by 777 ligature pairs for the Interlock style alone.
foundry_blurb: A retro font family embracing 70s and 80s disco music, coming with seven font families and special features such as stylistic alternates, swash and ligatures.

name: Deconeu
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Aprian Sembada, Cecep Nur Rohim
classification_notes: A single-weight display face combining Art Deco elegance with angular Gothic-adjacent stems; classed as display given its ornamental, headline-focused brief.
summary: A single-weight display face reworking Art Deco elegance with angular, faintly Gothic stems and a playful modern finish.
description: Deconeu combines Art Deco's timeless geometry with a playful pop-culture edge and a hint of Gothic angularity, giving it a sharp, retro-modern feel suited to headlines, logos and posters.
foundry_blurb: An Art Deco typeface gets a fresh, playful makeover, combining the timeless elegance of Art Deco with modern pop culture and a hint of Gothic to create something entirely new.

name: Gream
designer: Ricky Rinaldi, Aprian Sembada, Cecep Nur Rohim
classification_notes: A two-style blackletter face that softens traditional blackletter strokes with rounded, contemporary curves, explicitly framed by the foundry as a modern reworking of blackletter.
summary: A rounded, modern reworking of blackletter that blends sharp angular edges with soft curves, in Clean and distressed Rust cuts.
description: Gream reinterprets blackletter through softer, rounded shapes, keeping enough traditional angularity to read as blackletter while feeling contemporary. A Clean cut sits alongside a distressed Rust companion for a rougher finish.
foundry_blurb: A typeface that combines modernism with the playful curves of round shapes, blending sharp, angular edges with soft, rounded forms to redefine Blackletter in a fresh and contemporary way.
